chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When you go out from your house, say: 'In the Name of Allah, I rely upon Allah. There is neither might nor strength except with Allah. O Allah, I ask You for the goodness of what I am going out for, and I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I am going out for. O Allah, expand upon me from Your grace, and complete Your favor upon me, and employ me in Your obedience, and make my desire to be in what is with You, and cause me to die upon Your religion and the religion of Your Messenger (peace be upon him and his family).'

key_terms.لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّه: There is no might and no strength except with Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to recite when leaving the house in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this supplication serves as a daily spiritual anchor, transforming mundane departures into acts of worship by invoking reliance (tawakkul) and seeking divine facilitation. It reflects the Shia emphasis on integrating dhikr into daily routines, ensuring that one's intentions and actions remain aligned with the Prophet's tradition (sunnah) until death. The prayer specifically requests that one's desires be directed toward what is with God, highlighting the transition from worldly concerns to eternal readiness.
